businesses.platform_company: EmCare (ER staffing) + AmSurg (ambulatory surgery); KKR's equity was wiped out in the May 2023 Chapter 11 — now owned by former creditors

evidence.description: KKR took Envision private in 2018 in a $9.9B deal financed with ~$7B of debt (~70% of the price). When the No Surprises Act (2022) ended its lucrative out-of-network billing model, the debt load became unsustainable and Envision filed Chapter 11 in May 2023 — one of the largest PE-backed healthcare bankruptcies. KKR's equity was wiped out and creditors took control.

Envision's EmCare unit was a central driver of the US surprise-billing crisis. A Yale study (Cooper & Scott Morton) of 2.2M ER visits found out-of-network billing rates jumped sharply after EmCare took over hospital emergency rooms — at ~15% of hospitals out-of-network rates exceeded 80% — exposing in-network patients to large surprise bills.

businesses.platform_company: One of the largest US emergency-medicine and hospital physician staffing firms

evidence.description: US DOJ False Claims Act settlement ($60M, 2017): TeamHealth, as successor to IPC Healthcare, resolved allegations of 'upcoding' — billing Medicare, Medicaid, the Defense Health Agency and the federal employee program for higher and more expensive levels of service than were actually provided. Originated as a qui tam whistleblower suit; TeamHealth entered a 5-year Corporate Integrity Agreement.

ProPublica documented how TeamHealth, under Blackstone, used out-of-network emergency-room billing to mark up patient bills — a model that generated large surprise bills for insured patients who had no choice of ER physician.

businesses.platform_company: 4th-largest US emergency-medicine staffing firm (~258 emergency departments; 7,500+ clinicians across 36 states)
